title: Tracker shows how complete each item is, by lettered parts

C1.rule: Mechanical, one owned file, fully specified, no design choice

C2.rule: Bounded implementation or tests, clear spec, one or two owned files and their tests

C3.rule: Cross-module design; changes a gate or the ledger contract; wrong means every project inherits it

C4.rule: Planning, merging, reconciling, anything in a project's real data, a sponsor decision

phases.name: Parts
phases.goal: The ledger and tracker learn a part: a lettered sub-ticket of an item, with its own status, owner and share, so completion is measured instead of guessed.
phases.exit: A ledger item can carry parts, bin/tracker addresses them, the board renders the completion view above, warm-up counts them, every open item is migrated or confirmed as one whole part, and the naming standard is recorded as mandatory.

items.title: Ledger schema: parts on items, validated
items.what: A `parts` array on a ledger item: id `<ITEM>.<LETTER>` with letters in order and never reused, title, share (shares of an item's parts sum to 100), status (done / running / waiting / other), owner, optional `until` (a date, only with status waiting), optional `risk` (high/medium/low) with a `reason`. An item with no `parts` behaves as one part worth 100 -- tools/tracker/ledger.py computes completion the same way either way. Validation lives beside the existing item checks in ledger.py's validate().
items.done: validate() rejects a duplicate or out-of-order letter, shares that do not sum to 100, a status outside the vocabulary, a risk word without a reason, and a waiting part without `until`; accepts a wellformed parts array and an item with none. Tests red first.

log.event: merged in PR #227 lettered parts core, nesting and roll-up; builder gated with affected tests (machine saturated), full suite on merged main

items.title: bin/tracker set addresses a part
items.what: `bin/tracker set ITEM.A --status running --owner lead --until 2026-09-23 --risk medium --reason "..."` finds the part by its full id inside the item's `parts` array and updates it in place, the same way `bin/tracker set ITEM --status ...` already updates a whole item. Closing the last open part flips the item itself to done and logs it -- no separate step marks the item done.
items.done: Setting every part of an item to done closes the item and writes one log entry naming which part closed it last; setting a part on an item with no `parts` array is refused, naming P-05 as the fix (migrate first).

log.event: merged in PR #228 tracker set addresses a part; builder gated with affected tests (machine saturated), full suite on merged main

items.title: Board renders the completion view
items.what: tools/tracker/board.py replaces the rendered Lanes section with the view this proposal's mockup shows: summary tiles, a filter bar (group, proposal, owner, status, free-text search), features collapsed to one line (id, title, %, segmented bar, next open part), a click-to-expand parts table, and a 'show finished' toggle off by default. Static HTML with the ledger data embedded as JSON and a small inline script -- no build step, no external library. D5's answer decides whether the old share/cumulative table stays reachable as a folded 'advanced' section.
items.done: tracker board renders the new view for a ledger with parts and for one without; proposalcheck and the existing board tests still pass; a page with 90+ done items and 5 open renders under the same size budget board.py already enforces.

log.event: merged in PR #229 board completion overview, Lanes folded; builder gated with affected tests (machine saturated), full suite on merged main

items.title: Warm-up card and checkpoint count parts
items.what: bin/warmup's card and tools/tracker/checkpoint.py report completion the same way: an item with open parts shows its %, not just 'in progress'; the card's per-project summary counts parts toward what is pending, not whole items only.
items.done: A ledger with a part-carrying item shows that item's % on the card and in the checkpoint; a ledger with none renders exactly as it does today (no regression).

log.event: Warm-up card and checkpoint show completion % and next part; merged in #234. Recorded late: the branch landed but the row was never moved.

items.title: Migrate the open items into parts
items.what: Every open item across the 10 ledgers (W-10, L-07, L-02, S-07, S-08, and whatever is open by the time this runs) gets a `parts` array reflecting real, current sub-work -- read from its own log, not invented -- or is confirmed as one whole part worth 100 when it genuinely has no sub-work. This is the one-time data migration; P-02 is the tool it uses.
tests: bin/tracker validate on every migrated ledger
items.done: Every ledger in the project validates clean; every open item either has a `parts` array whose shares sum to 100, or is confirmed (in its log) as a single whole part; nothing that was `done` is touched.

log.event: merged in PR #230 W-10, L-02, L-07, S-07, S-08 split into parts; builder gated with affected tests (machine saturated), full suite on merged main

items.title: Standard change entry and docs
items.what: A `Standard change (mandatory):` CHANGELOG.md entry naming the parts schema, the naming standard (`<ITEM>.<LETTER>`, letters in order and never reused, a part is a sub-ticket, an item with no parts is one part worth 100), and that it replaces the Lanes overview as what the tracker page shows by default. HANDOFF.md / docs/OPERATING-RULES.md gain the naming standard in the read order.
items.done: CHANGELOG.md carries the mandatory entry; a project run through bin/rulecheck after P-01 through P-05 land and before this one reports behind on it; after, it reports current.

log.event: merged in PR #231 standard change entry, templates and skills; builder gated with affected tests (machine saturated), full suite on merged main

items.title: Progress over time, computed from git history
items.what: tools/tracker/history.py walks the ledgers' git history and counts tickets added, closed and completion per day, cached; bin/tracker history prints it; svg() renders two inline charts. Nothing is updated by hand.
items.done: Daily series from the first ledger commit to today, tickets counted at every part depth, cache reuse, two charts; tests on a temp git repo.

items.title: The proposal tree is the top view: proposal, then items, then parts
items.what: The sponsor: "at the top, there should be like proposal nineteen. And when I expand it, then there should be P1, P2, P3. And then when I expand P1, then there should be P1, A, B, C, D." and "I want to track the proposals, you know, the proposals is six out of six done. But the subtasks are more. So I want the proposals to have drop down." The drill-down exists but sits under the group lists, so the first thing he sees is items grouped by finish now / back burner / waiting rather than his proposals. Put the proposal tree directly under the tiles and charts, and fold the group lists below it.
items.done: The page opens on proposal rows, each showing N of N items done and a percentage; one click expands to items, another to parts, another to sub-parts; the group lists are still reachable, folded, below.

items.title: A second button switches the tracker to Kanban
items.what: The sponsor: "and I and then there could be a sec second button which can switch to the Kanban style." A view switch beside the existing filters: the proposal tree, or a Kanban board of columns by status with one card per item.
items.done: Two buttons switch the view with no page reload and no server round trip; the Kanban columns are the ledger's own statuses; each card names its item, its proposal and its completion; the choice survives a reload for that viewer; both views work in light and dark mode and at phone width.
